newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest crime wave may be waning, chief says.
newsitem.headline: Budapest crime wave may be waning, chief says.

text.p: A crime wave which hit the Hungarian capital over the past year may be coming to end, Budapest police chief Attila Berta said on Monday.
Berta said the total number of crimes in Budapest dropped by six percent in the first half of 1997 compared with the same period of 1996.
"This is a very fragile result, but it is a beginning," he told a news conference.
He added that public safety in Budapest was crucial because it affected Hungary's image abroad.
Budapest was hit last autumn by a wave of gangland warfare with a series of shootings, grenade and petrol bomb explosions killing almost 20 people.
In May and June police closed down a number of Budapest restaurants for overcharging patrons.

Berta said the number of street patrols rose by 33 percent in the first half of 1997, the police force grew by 800 officers on street duty and "Delfin", a 130-strong rapid intervention motorcycle unit, proved an instant hit.
Although Budapest accounts for only one-fifth of the Hungary's 10.4 million population, one third of the crimes and about half of all car thefts are committed here.
